question: The Green Revolution within India led to an increase in agricultural production, especially in ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Haryana, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Punjab**, where it was first introduced, the **Green Revolution** led to significant increases in the **state's agrarian affair, **supporting India's overall frugality.
 
• The **Green Revolution was the emergence of new kinds of crops, specifically wheat and rice varietals, that were suitable to double if not triadic product of those crops in two countries **
 
• The **Green Revolution **within India led to an increase in agrarian products, especially in **Haryana, Punjab, and Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• Major mileposts in this undertaking were the development of a high-yielding variety of seeds of wheat and rust-resistant strains of wheat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The crop area under high-yielding kinds of wheat and rice grew vastly during the Green Revolution. 
 
• **The Green Revolution in India was initiated in the 1960s by introducing high-yielding kinds of rice and wheat to increase food products in order to palliate hunger and poverty. **
 
• **The term green revolution was first used by William Gaud and Norman Borlaug is the Father of the Green Revolution. **
 
• In the time** 1965, the government of India launched the Green Revolution with the help of a geneticist, now known as the father of the Green revolution( India)M.S. Swaminathan. **
 
• The **Green Revolution**, or the Agricultural Revolution (after the Neolithic Revolution and the British Agricultural Revolution), is the set of studies on generation switch initiatives happening between 1950 and the late Nineteen Sixties.
 
• It became **associated with chemical fertilizers, agrochemicals, controlled water-deliver** (generally concerning irrigation), and greater current techniques of cultivation, which consist of mechanization.
 
• One leader has become agricultural scientist **Norman Borlaug, the "Father of the Green Revolution",** who acquired the **Nobel Peace Prize in 1970. **
